questions.question: What distinguishes an execution plan from a to-do list?
options: A dependency graph with evidence and proof
questions.explanation: Dependencies, receipts, and completion proof make the plan executable and resumable.

questions.question: Why define a shared contract before its implementations?
options: So dependent surfaces do not invent conflicting behavior
So only one agent can work
questions.explanation: A fixed contract unblocks safe parallel work on dependent surfaces.

questions.question: What does a dependency cycle usually reveal?
options: A hidden unresolved decision or bad decomposition
questions.explanation: Cyclic work items cannot establish a valid starting point.

questions.question: When can two work items share an execution wave?
options: When their dependencies are complete and they are otherwise independent
When they touch the same files
questions.explanation: A wave contains all currently unblocked independent work.

questions.question: Why attach evidence to each work item?
options: To show why the change belongs and let new evidence revise it
questions.explanation: Evidence must justify and be capable of changing the plan.

questions.question: What makes a plan resumable?
options: Small items with status, artifacts, dependencies, and proof
questions.explanation: Durable item state lets another session continue without rediscovery.
